final_message:
The September 2026 draft for Bluebird Bakery is done, with 8 commentary bullets in section 1. Every number in the commentary traces back to the script's report or data file: 47 matched, 0 unmatched, 20 ignored as dates or counts. The DRAFT banner is still on.

**Files** (in `evals/runs/commit3-run-20261012/f_bb_from_zero_label/skill_output/`):
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.md`: the report, with the commentary filled in
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.json`: the source data for every number

**Data quality: one mismatch.** In March 2026, the "Total for Professional Services" row says 2,225.00, but the lines under it add up to 2,200.00 (a 25.00 gap). The analysis uses the line items, and the reviewer decides which figure is right. The commentary opens with this. Two other notes:
- The structure was partly rebuilt: "Total Delivery" had no heading row, and "Charitable Donations" had no total row.
- September isn't flagged as a partial month.

**Main points:**
- **Revenue was 81,300**, up 17.7% on August (69,050) and 17.3% above the prior 6-month average (69,292). Most of the rise is from a new stream, Wholesale Accounts, at 12,000. There's no comparison with September last year because the export only covers 9 months.
- **Gross margin was 65.3%**, up 5.7 points on August and the best month in the period.
- **Operating expenses were 31,570 (+21.0%).** All of the increase is Wages & Salaries, which went from 16,000 to 21,000 after being 16,000 every month this year. The reviewer needs to say whether that's a new level or a one-off.
- **Cash in Bank Accounts was 37,600**, down 1,800 on August and 10,800 on six months earlier, even though every month was profitable. Equity also fell. The data doesn't show why, so the commentary leaves that question for the reviewer.

The report table shows Mystery Shopper Program as "from 0", but it isn't a new cost. It was also 400 in March and June, so it looks quarterly, and the commentary says so.

**Uncategorised expenses:** three accounts matched no category rule and are grouped under "Other Opex": Instagram Ads, Mystery Shopper Program and Supplier Rebates.

I didn't add a `commentary.md` file to the case folder, which the eval runner's provenance step looks for. I ran the check directly on the report's commentary instead.
